statement: Node state updates carry a locally persisted monotonic boot incarnation through the schema, control-plane field, and publication path, with receiver-side fencing at the watermark check, missing-row upsert, and WebSocket identification slot, so stale-incarnation writers are refused with a typed terminal STALE_NODE_INCARNATION outcome.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

The incarnation must be minted from a locally persisted monotonic boot counter in the rejoin hints, not only from the bootstrap response, because idempotent same-address rejoin bypasses fresh admission.

The fence must be enforced at the receiver: the update predicate and watermark comparison in replica-dispatch-state-publication.js, the tryBootstrapMissingNodeStateUpdateRow upsert path, and the WebSocket transport handleIdentification slot; the existing boot-time self-applied clusterIncarnationFence remains but is not the mechanism under test.
A stale incarnation must produce a typed STALE_NODE_INCARNATION refusal classified as terminal, because the publisher retries generic errors forever.

The Math.max(requestedHeartbeatAt, now) clamp at replica-dispatch-state-publication.js must not lift a stale-incarnation writer's heartbeat to receiver-time; the incarnation comparison happens before the watermark comparison.
Each new regression test must fail when the corresponding incarnation check is reverted while the rest of the change remains.
